failure_summary.description: Picked an inflated option (hub plus an unproved rider) over the plain hub: 'least energy', an explicit V^lambda coefficient, 'free factor, rank >= 2n-2', or Sum N_c < infinity forcing a finite family.
Picked a weakened neighbour of the hub: one-way 'if exists then c in K' instead of iff, or a bare 'some C>0' after 'for every u' instead of C=C(p,q,n).
Chose a tautological iff ('invariant iff constant on the family'), which does not use the stem's named objects (the foci), over the theorem-bearing option.
Reverse-mathematics equivalence (Sigma^1_1 vs Sigma^1_2 induction): knowledge-bound, but the correct option was still the hub of the option set.

patch.reasoning: In all 8 failures the correct option is the hub: every other option is one corruption of it (a swap, an added rider, a deleted qualifier, a shifted index or exponent), while the chosen option is a one-sided extension or truncation of the hub at edit distance 2 from most of the others. The existing hub test (step 8) is buried and says only 'override on positive evidence'. Strength-ladder and 'strongest' wording then pull the agent to the most elaborate option, and 'iff beats one-way' and 'prefer a stronger option' pull it the wrong way. The previous restructure also deleted useful content, so this patch keeps it. It adds a short, countable hub procedure at the top that is robust to whether the truth is plain or carries a derivable Moreover clause, and states one direction per relation type: rider, deleted qualifier or converse, and tautology. It repairs the tie-breaker line that told the agent to distrust any 'dependence list', which led to the bare 'C>0' pick. It also shortens the odd-one-out bullet and the step 8 text, which are now covered by STEP 0.

edits.content:
## STEP 0 (visible, first): find the hub by edit-count
Distractors are mostly single corruptions of the TRUE option, so they sit one edit from the truth and two or more edits from each other. For every option, count how many other options differ from it by ONE edit: add or drop a clause or rider, swap two symbols or index placements, shift an exponent, constant or range, change a quantifier or hypothesis, flip a direction, 'iff' vs 'if', 'C=C(p,q,n)' vs 'some C'. Write the counts (A:k B:k ...). The option with the highest count is the hub and your default answer, whether or not it is the longest, strongest or most elaborate. A neighbour that only extends or truncates the hub has count about 1 and is never promoted by 'it implies the hub' or by the stem word 'strongest'.
- Leave the hub only if one of its clauses FAILS a concrete test (invariant, degenerate case, zero data, generic infinite family). The strength ladder ranks only options that survive this step.
- Hub vs its extension (hub + clause): the extension wins only if the clause is a one-line consequence or a 'Moreover, if H (stated inside the option) then C'. A clause adding a coefficient or asymptotic expansion, minimality ('least energy'), structure ('free factor', 'unique'), or an 'in addition' property of the constructed object is a rider, so the hub wins.
- Hub vs its truncation (hub minus content): the truncation loses when the dropped content is the converse of an iff (iff beats 'if ... then necessarily'), the dependence of a constant on the stem's own parameters (a bare 'there exists C>0' after 'for every u' lets C depend on u), a smoothness or range clause, or a qualifier. The same applies to a count condition that forces finiteness (positive integers N_c with Sum N_c < infinity).
- An option that restates a definition ('invariant iff constant on the family') or never uses the objects the stem names is a tautology, not the theorem. Reject it.
Then write the three PRIORITY lines (finalists = hub and its nearest neighbour).

edits.target: Locate the hub, the option from which every other option follows by one small edit (add or drop a clause, swap two symbols, shift an exponent, reverse a direction). The true statement is usually the hub, or the hub plus a clause you can actually derive. Override the hub only on positive evidence.
edits.content: Use the STEP 0 hub count. The true statement is the hub, or the hub plus a clause you can actually derive. Override the hub only when a concrete test falsifies one of its clauses.

edits.target: (iv) contains no explicit rate, constant, or dependence list that you cannot derive.
edits.content: (iv) contains no explicit rate, numeric coefficient or expansion term that you cannot derive. A dependence list naming only the stem's own structural parameters (C=C(p,q,n)) is part of the plain theorem. Its omission (a bare 'some C>0' after 'for every solution u') lets C depend on u and is the weakened variant.

edits.target: count how many options use each placement. If one option is the isolated swap and all others agree on the other placement, the swap is the corruption (distractors are single edits of the truth and so mostly inherit its details).
edits.content: apply the STEP 0 count to that single detail: the isolated swap is the corruption.
